## Natural history notes

A medium-sized seed bug characterized by a slender red to orange body, dark wing markings, long legs, and a narrow piercing beak. In Florida, the Common Cotton Stainer Bug is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, hammocks, forest edges, and disturbed areas where cotton, hibiscus, mallow, and related host plants occur. Adults and nymphs feed on seeds, fruits, and developing plant tissue, especially in the mallow family, and can stain cotton or damage seed crops while also serving as prey for birds, spiders, assassin bugs, and other predators.
